propositions.name: ether_fills_all_space
propositions.statement: A medium called the ether exists, whose vibrations produce the phenomena of heat and light, and which fills all space.
propositions.quote: The undulatory theory of light assumes the existence of a medium called the ether, whose vibrations produce the phenomena of heat and light, and which is supposed to fill all space.

propositions.name: ether_at_rest_earth_moves
propositions.statement: The ether is at rest and the earth is moving through it.
propositions.quote: Assuming then that the ether is at rest, the earth moving through it, the time required for light to pass from one point to another on the earth’s surface, would depend on the direction in which it travels.

propositions.name: time_required_is_a_quantity
propositions.statement: The time required for light to pass from one point to another on the earth's surface is a quantity that has a value depending on direction.
propositions.quote: Assuming then that the ether is at rest, the earth moving through it, the time required for light to pass from one point to another on the earth’s surface, would depend on the direction in which it travels.

propositions.name: fresnel_drag_in_optical_media
propositions.statement: The ether enclosed in optical media partakes of the motion of these media to an extent depending on their indices of refraction.
propositions.quote: According to Fresnel, the ether, which is enclosed in optical media, partakes of the motion of these media, to an extent depending on their indices of refraction.

propositions.name: air_drag_negligible
propositions.statement: The motion of the ether within the air is a small fraction of the motion of the air itself and will be neglected.
propositions.quote: For air, this motion would be but a small fraction of that of the air itself and will be neglected.

propositions.name: return_path_loses_signal
propositions.statement: Any measurement of the velocity of light at the earth's surface that returns the light over its path loses nearly as much as was gained in going.
propositions.quote: we have thus far no method for measuring the velocity of light which does not involve the necessity of returning the light over its path, whereby it would lose nearly as much as was gained in going.

propositions.name: squared_ratio_effect_too_small_without_wavelength
propositions.statement: The difference depending on the square of the ratio of the two velocities is far too small to measure without a wave-length standard.
propositions.quote: The difference depending on the square of the ratio of the two velocities, according to Maxwell, is far too small to measure.

propositions.name: wavelength_yellow_light_as_standard
propositions.statement: With a wave-length of yellow light as a standard, the quantity — if it exists — is easily measurable.
propositions.quote: The following is intended to show that, with a wave-length of yellow light as a standard, the quantity — if it exists — is easily measurable.

propositions.name: perpendicular_light_unaffected
propositions.statement: Light that travels in a direction at right angles to the earth's motion is entirely unaffected by that motion.
propositions.quote: If, however, the light had traveled in a direction at right angles to the earth’s motion it would be entirely unaffected

propositions.name: orbital_speed_gives_ratio_v_over_V
propositions.statement: The velocity of the earth in its orbit gives a ratio v/V approximately equal to 1/10000.
propositions.quote: Considering only the velocity of the earth in its orbit, the ratio

propositions.name: two_pencils_at_right_angles_interfere
propositions.statement: An apparatus can be constructed so as to permit two pencils of light which have traveled over paths at right angles to each other to interfere, with the pencil in the direction of the earth's motion traveling farther.
propositions.quote: an apparatus is so constructed as to permit two pencils of light, which have traveled over paths at right angles to each other, to interfere, the pencil which has traveled in the direction of the earth’s motion

propositions.name: rotation_lengthens_second_pencil_path
propositions.statement: Revolving the apparatus through 90° brings the second pencil into the direction of the earth's motion so that its path lengthens.
propositions.quote: If, now, the apparatus be revolved through 90° so that the second pencil is brought into the direction of the earth’s motion, its path will have lengthened

propositions.name: equal_geometric_paths_between_arms
propositions.statement: The distance bc is made equal to bd, and a plate of glass g compensates for the thickness of b, so the two rays traverse equal paths and are in condition to interfere.
propositions.quote: The distance bc being made equal to bd , and a plate of glass g being interposed in the path of the ray bc , to compensate for the thickness of the glass b , which is traversed by the ray bd , the two rays will have traveled over equal paths and are in condition to interfere.

propositions.name: apparatus_movable_about_vertical_axis
propositions.statement: The whole apparatus, including the lamp and the telescope, is movable about a vertical axis.
propositions.quote: The whole apparatus, including the lamp and the telescope, was movable about a vertical axis.

propositions.name: earth_orbital_motion_toward_hercules
propositions.statement: Early in April the earth's motion in its orbit coincides roughly in longitude with the estimated direction of the motion of the solar system toward the constellation Hercules.
propositions.quote: At this time of the year, early in April, the earth’s motion in its orbit coincides roughly in longitude with the estimated direction of the motion of the solar system — namely, toward the constellation Hercules.

propositions.name: motions_combine_as_components_with_resultant
propositions.statement: The earth's orbital motion and the sun's motion combine as two components whose resultant has a definite direction.
propositions.quote: The nearer the two components are in magnitude to each other, the more nearly would their resultant coincide with the plane of the equator.

propositions.name: arm_pointing_east_coincides_with_resultant
propositions.statement: If the apparatus is placed with arms pointing north and east at noon, the arm pointing east coincides with the resultant motion and the other is at right angles.
propositions.quote: In this case, if the apparatus be so placed that the arms point north and east at noon, the arm pointing east would coincide with the resultant motion, and the other would be at right angles.

propositions.name: brass_arms_expand_with_temperature
propositions.statement: The arms are of brass with coefficient of expansion 0.000019 and length about 1000 mm or 1 700 000 wave-lengths, so a temperature difference of one one-hundredth of a degree between arms displaces the fringes three times the sought amount.
propositions.quote: These being of brass whose coefficient of expansion is 0.000019 and having a length of about 1000 mm. or 1 700 000 wave-lengths, if one arm should have a temperature only one one-hundredth of a degree higher than the other, the fringes would thereby experience a displacement three times as great as that which would result from the rotation.

propositions.name: temperature_changes_direction_independent
propositions.statement: Changes of temperature are independent of the direction of the arms, so their effect on the fringes can be eliminated.
propositions.quote: On the other hand, since the changes of temperature are independent of the direction of the arms, if these changes were not too great their effect could be eliminated.

propositions.name: apparatus_geometry_stable_under_rotation
propositions.statement: Apart from bending of the arms during rotation, the geometry of the apparatus remains fixed as it revolves.
propositions.quote: It was found, however, that the displacement on account of bending of the arms during rotation was so considerable that the instrument had to be returned to the maker, with instructions to make it revolve as easily as possible.

propositions.name: target_signal_is_periodic_variation
propositions.statement: The effect being sought is a periodic variation of the fringe positions with the rotation of the apparatus, distinguishable from a gradual change.
propositions.quote: This gradual change, which should not in the least affect the periodic variation for which we are searching, would of itself necessitate an outstanding error

propositions.name: telescope_direction_labels_the_data
propositions.statement: The direction toward which the telescope points can be given by compass-point headings for each column of observations.
propositions.quote: The heading of the columns in the table gives the direction toward which the telescope pointed.

propositions.name: fringe_positions_are_measurable_scalars
propositions.statement: The position of the center of the dark fringe can be recorded in twelfths of the distance between the fringes.
propositions.quote: The numbers in the columns are the positions of the center of the dark fringe in twelfths of the distance between the fringes.

propositions.name: null_displacement_refutes_stationary_ether
propositions.statement: The absence of any displacement of the interference bands shows the hypothesis of a stationary ether to be incorrect and erroneous.
propositions.quote: The interpretation of these results is that there is no displacement of the interference bands. The result of the hypothesis of a stationary ether is thus shown to be incorrect, and the necessary conclusion follows that the hypothesis is erroneous.

propositions.name: aberration_previously_required_moving_earth_still_ether
propositions.statement: The hitherto generally accepted explanation of aberration presupposes that the earth moves through the ether, the latter remaining at rest.
propositions.quote: This conclusion directly contradicts the explanation of the phenomenon of aberration which has been hitherto generally accepted, and which presupposes that the earth moves through the ether, the latter remaining at rest.

propositions.name: decisive_experiment_between_theories_possible
propositions.statement: The two theories of aberration can be put to the test of a decisive experiment.
propositions.quote: Still it would have been satisfactory, if it had been possible to have put the two theories to the test of some decisive experiment.
